items.title: Development and Preliminary Psychometric Evaluation of a Digital-Intelligence Literacy Self-Report Scale Among Students in Medical and Health-Related Programs
items.abstract: Medical students increasingly engage with interconnected digital systems, health data, and artificial intelligence (AI), but existing instruments vary in the aspects of digital, data, and AI literacy they assess in medical contexts. This study developed and initially evaluated the Chinese-language Digital-Intelligence Literacy Scale for Medical Students (DIL-MS). Following two rounds of consultation with 16 experts, a 34-item questionnaire was field-tested at one Chinese university. Of 1118 returned questionnaires, 710 were analyzed in non-overlapping exploratory (n = 344) and confirmatory (n = 366) subsamples. Full-pool exploratory factor analysis and confirmatory factor analysis for ordinal data informed a revised 32-item scale across six domains: readiness, theoretical literacy, application skills, health data practices and interpretation, critical thinking, and ethical literacy. Parallel analysis suggested six factors, with some item assignments differing from the proposed domains. The correlated six-factor model fit better than the tested five-, four-, and single-factor alternatives, but absolute fit was limited (robust comparative fit index = 0.802; robust root mean square error of approximation = 0.090). Overall Cronbach’s α was 0.938, and domain α ranged from 0.726 to 0.871; convergent and discriminant validity evidence varied across domains. The DIL-MS provides medically contextualized self-report content for exploring perceived learning needs and mapping curricula.

items.title: Development and preliminary validation of an AI acceptance scale for intercultural teaching and its cross-sectional associations with university teachers’ occupational wellbeing
items.abstract: Background University teachers’ occupational wellbeing and emotional exhaustion are relevant occupational-health concerns in higher education. As generative artificial intelligence becomes embedded in teaching work, AI acceptance may represent a perceived, context-specific appraisal of whether AI is usable for intercultural teaching tasks. This study developed a preliminary measure of AI acceptance for intercultural teaching and examined its cross-sectional associations with teacher resources and occupational-health indicators. Methods This two-sample cross-sectional study used Sample A to examine the empirical behavior of the AI Acceptance for Intercultural Teaching Scale and Sample B to test measurement validity and occupational health associations. IBM SPSS Statistics 27.0.1 was used for descriptive statistics, EFA, Cronbach’s alpha, correlations, and regression analyses. CFA and SEM were conducted in R 4.6.1 (lavaan 0.6.21, lavaan.mi 0.1.0, and mice 3.19.0) using robust maximum likelihood (MLR) estimation; CR and AVE were calculated from standardized CFA loadings, and HTMT from item correlations. Hypothesis tests used non-imputed scale-score regressions; multiple imputation (mice, m = 5) with D2-pooled CFA/SEM model tests served as sensitivity analysis, and indirect-association bootstrap intervals were sensitivity summaries rather than formal D2-pooled tests. Results The AITA items were suitable for factor analysis in Sample A (KMO = 0.940), but the exploratory loading pattern did not cleanly reproduce the theorized four TAM-based dimensions. In Sample B, the overall AITA score showed good internal consistency (alpha = 0.858), whereas the four subdimensions showed substantial overlap and weaker reliability and convergent-validity evidence. AI acceptance was positively associated with intercultural teaching self-efficacy and autonomous teaching motivation. Self-efficacy was associated with both occupational wellbeing and lower emotional exhaustion, whereas autonomous motivation was associated primarily with occupational wellbeing. Direct associations between AI acceptance and the occupational-health outcomes were not significant. Conclusion The present findings provide preliminary evidence for using the overall AITA score as a context-specific measure of AI acceptance in intercultural teaching. The results also show cross-sectional associations between AI acceptance and teacher-resource variables, but they do not establish causal effects, mediation, or intervention effectiveness. The four TAM-based dimensions should be treated as provisional content facets requiring further validation.
